messages.subject: setting up classifiers
parts:
Hi, seeking help!

I am quite new to R/geomorph and recently all my code seemed to stop working with error messages when I tried to run (previously working) functions. I seem to have resolved most of this but I cannot get the classifier from CSV to work. It seems to not be recognising the headers as wont set them as a factor?! Sure there is just something I am not seeing. Any suggestions would be appreciated!  Many thanks. 

Here is an example of the classifier CSV: 
SpecID species breed sex period type
Sp1 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs
Sp2 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs
Sp3 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs
Sp4 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Pleictocene Aurochs
Sp5 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Pleictocene Aurochs
Sp6 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown EarlyHolocene Aurochs
Sp7 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs
Sp8 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Pleictocene Aurochs
Sp9 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs
Sp10 Bprimigenius Aurochs Unknown Unknown Aurochs



I am running the code below:

> classifier<-read.csv("my classifier.csv", header = T, row.names = 1)
> is.factor(classifier$species)
[1] FALSE

messages.author: 4fbf3c0920d27309
messages.subject: Re: setting up classifiers
parts:
So to add I think I have solved this with :

> #load classifiers from csv
> classifier <- read.csv("my classifier.csv", header=T, row.names=1)
> species <- factor(classifier$species)
> is.factor(species) # check that it is a factor
[1] TRUE

messages.author: 7df8f899a4df294b
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: setting up classifiers
parts:
Hi Ewan,

 

By setting header=T and row.names=1, you end up with one too many factors. You should be able to get the column headers recognised as factors by:

 

1)

> classifier<-read.csv("my classifier.csv", header = T)

#classifier$SpecID should be recognised as a factor, and there will be no rownames

 

Or

2)

>classifier<-read.csv("my classifier.csv", skip=1, row.names = 1) #skips first row of csv file

>colnames(classifier)<-c(‘species’, ’breed’, ’sex’, ‘period’, ‘type’) #adds column names ‘manually’

#classifier$species should now be recognised as a factor, as there will be 5 columns of data/5 named columns

 

 

Or

3)

Have csv as:

species breed    sex         period   type

Sp1         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs

Sp2         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs

Sp3         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs

Sp4         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Pleictocene        Aurochs

Sp5         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Pleictocene        Aurochs

Sp6         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            EarlyHolocene   Aurochs

Sp7         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs

Sp8         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Pleictocene        Aurochs

Sp9         Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs

Sp10      Bprimigenius      Aurochs               Unknown            Unknown            Aurochs
>classifier<-read.csv("my classifier.csv", header = T, row.names = 1)

Should work as you want, as you’ll have 5 columns of data/5 named columns

 

Best,

Ana Serra Silva
